subtype: Approach: recognising own limits and referring on [Revision]
passage:
Alka: Madhav bhaiya, can I ask something about robotics? I want to build a small arm
Madhav: honestly I don't know robotics at all
Alka: oh. I thought you knew everything in tech
Madhav: no way 😄 I know software. I'd only be guessing about motors and control, and that might send you the wrong way
Alka: so what should I do?
Madhav: there's a senior, Mihir, in the mechatronics group. I'll message him now and introduce you
Alka: that would be great
Madhav: done. he said Thursday after lunch. ask him about starter kits
Alka: thank you bhaiya. I'm glad you said that instead of bluffing
Madhav: I'll still help with the coding part once you have the arm

qa.q: Which field did Alka ask Madhav about?
qa.a: Alka asked Madhav about robotics, wanting to build a small arm.

qa.q: Why did Madhav say the honest answer instead of guessing?
qa.a: Madhav worried that guessing about motors and control might send Alka the wrong way, so it was better to admit the limit.

qa.q: What could Alka do to prepare for meeting Mihir, and why?
qa.a: Alka could write two or three questions about starter kits first, because a short list makes the meeting more useful.

qa.q: How might Alka feel about Madhav's honesty?
qa.a: Alka felt glad, since Alka says it is good that Madhav did not bluff and gets a real introduction instead.

grounding: When a junior asks about a field the mentor does not know, the mentor says so and introduces a senior from that field.
